trends.what: A curated list of free APIs for developers to use in their projects.
trends.why: It's a massive, constantly updated reference that saves developers hours of searching for free data sources.

trends.what: An open-source platform offering free coding lessons, projects, and certifications in math, programming, and computer science.
trends.why: It's the go-to free resource for self-taught developers, and its curriculum updates keep it relevant.

trends.what: A massive collection of freely available programming books and learning resources in multiple languages.
trends.why: It democratizes access to technical knowledge, making it a staple bookmark for learners worldwide.

trends.what: A personal AI assistant that runs on any OS and platform, designed to be your always-available helper.
trends.why: The 'lobster way' branding and cross-platform promise tap into the growing demand for local, private AI assistants.

trends.what: Interactive roadmaps and guides that help developers plan their learning paths and career growth.
trends.why: With tech careers evolving fast, people crave structured visual guidance, and this repo delivers it beautifully.

trends.what: A tool that makes AI agents generate minimal, lazy-but-correct code, mimicking a senior dev who avoids over-engineering.
trends.why: It's a humorous yet practical take on AI code quality, resonating with devs tired of bloated AI-generated code.

trends.what: A fullscreen, mouse-interactive terminal UI and harness for running coding agents, built by SpaceXAI.
trends.why: It brings a polished, IDE-like experience to terminal-based AI coding, which is a hot niche right now.

trends.what: A pure-C, zero-dependency runtime that runs frontier mixture-of-experts AI models on consumer hardware by streaming experts from disk.
trends.why: It promises to run huge models locally without expensive GPUs, a breakthrough for privacy and cost-conscious users.
